process: Not level-based (one continuous six-section course), so no retrofit. One independent review round found no BLOCKING or MEDIUM issue, so the game is unchanged; the record adds a short browser check.
independentProbes: The reviewer's reaction-limited bot, reading only public state with lagged traffic, finished 20 of 20 races at 0.25 s and 0.35 s at 60 Hz (87-110 s on the 120 s clock), also when limited to the 33 m of road on screen, and 19-20 of 20 at 30 and 120 Hz. Idle, mash, random keys and hold-plus-alternate patterns from 0.1 to 4 s won 0% over 30 seeds; holding only the throttle wins 21.3% over 300 seeds, under the 25% cap. Exactly one end fires, the terminal state freezes, play matches across 30, 60 and 120 Hz, a 20,000-step hostile-input fuzz stayed finite, random driving never overlapped or tunnelled through traffic, and steering into the rail never stalls the car.
openNotes: Holding only the throttle finishes 21% of races, a thin margin under the 25% cap.
The screen shows about 33 m of road ahead, roughly 0.8 s at top speed; bots limited to that view still won every race.
The 1,070-line source is above the 800-line guideline but is organised into clear blocks (route data, collision, physics, spawning, tick, drawing).
There are no rival racers, only traffic.

browser.method: Official Claude in Chrome extension, local server; a real click on Start, synthetic in-page keys; only DOM text and the canvas were read.
observed: Chinese: Start opened section 1/6 (果园) with condition 4/4 and the 120 s clock; holding the throttle for 4 s drove 32 m at 56 km/h with the HUD, road and car unobscured.
The batch 2 acceptance record covers the English desktop run, a loss, restart and the Chinese phone frame with touch controls.
